Highly detailed value-chain agents, data, optimisation, validation, sensitivity analysis, supplementary model documentation and explicit limitations.
Clear multi-agent architecture and roles, public data/code, baseline and ablation evaluation, and extensive limitations/validation discussion.
Detailed agents, auction mechanism, equations/pseudocode, datasets, multi-scenario/cross-country evaluation and explicit limitations/future work.
Detailed hierarchical agents, MQTT/negotiation mechanisms, real district data, simulation/field implementation, equations, scenarios and explicit limitations.
Clear objective, decentralized agent/MPC design, detailed field-derived data/model parameters, strong comparative simulation and explicit computational/robustness limitations.

Clear hierarchical coordinator/local-agent roles and directed communication, detailed training/evaluation setup, multiple baselines, quantitative results and explicit scalability/generalization limitations.

Clear greenhouse-agent/attention architecture, detailed equations, hyperparameters, real climate inputs and baseline comparisons; limitations are discussed mainly through research challenges/future extensions rather than a dedicated comprehensive limitations analysis.

Detailed Family/Herd agents, socio-ecological environment, data assumptions and multi-scenario simulation; interactions are largely environment-mediated without a formal coordination protocol; limitations and extensions are explicit.

Detailed farm and auctioneer/advisor roles, double-auction coordination, algorithms/pseudocode/hyperparameters, two-country datasets, baselines/ablations and extensive deployment limitations/future work.

Clear socio-ecological objective, farmer/environment agent roles, rich Malawi survey/spatial data, explicit validation/sensitivity analysis, public code/data and detailed limitations; inter-agent communication/coordination is mainly indirect through shared environmental/social feedback rather than a clearly specified protocol.

Clear MAELIA objective, detailed farmer/dam/state-service roles and regulatory coordination, rich stakeholder/GIS/hydrology inputs and strong architecture description; evaluation is primarily calibration/sensitivity with application results deferred to other papers, and limitations are discussed mainly as calibration challenges.

Clear research questions and herder/farmer rule-based roles, but this short proposed-work paper provides only a preliminary synthetic simulation, limited empirical/data detail, no implementation platform/code, partial interaction specification and no meaningful limitations discussion.

Clear six-agent JADE architecture and ACL coordination with well-described query workflows, but the prototype uses simple predefined examples, lacks a formal dataset/baseline/quantitative evaluation, provides only partial reproducibility detail and frames its main constraints through future work.

Clear farmer-agent roles, explicit auction negotiation protocols, detailed Canterbury/FAO/cost inputs, repeated comparative simulations and reproducible auction logic; limitations/future extensions are present but less comprehensive than the other methodological sections.

Clear vulnerability/LCA objective, differentiated active/decision/reactive/passive agent roles, rich historical/government/producer/sugar-mill inputs and substantial sensitivity/LCA evaluation. Coordination is described mainly as information flow through system-dynamics networks rather than a formal protocol, and limitations are only partly explicit; no reproducibility package is provided.

Clear QML-MARL objective, specialised crop-resource agents, CTDE coordination and comparative baseline experiments. However, the reported farm/IoT environment is synthetic, generation details and implementation artefacts are limited, no code/data package is provided, and real IoT/live-farm validation and quantum/edge constraints are deferred to future work.

Clear agricultural task-allocation objective, heterogeneous robot/UAV roles, explicit centralized coalition assignment and Wi-Fi communication, detailed ACO equations/parameters and repeated simulations plus a five-robot proof of concept. Limitations are mainly expressed through future-work needs rather than a dedicated threats/limitations analysis.

Clear water-allocation objective, autonomous seller/bidder farm roles and explicit fixed-price/sealed-bid negotiation. Crop-water/pricing equations, scarcity scenarios and comparative experiments are sufficiently detailed for understanding/reproduction; limitations are only partially discussed through simplified indivisible water lots and future auction extensions.

Clear integrated irrigation/crop-health objective, detailed local/coordinator agent roles, trust-aware neighbour communication and consensus, explicit simulation/data sources, extensive baseline/ablation/cross-region evaluation and reproducible algorithm/parameter descriptions. The paper also explicitly states simulation-only irrigation validation and discusses field, noise, scaling and deployment limitations/future work.

Clear integrated MAELIA objective, detailed farmer/state-service roles and resource-mediated water coordination, rich empirical/GIS inputs and strong model description; evaluation is preliminary with calibration still ongoing, and limitations are discussed mainly through data/calibration challenges.

Clear hierarchical coordinator/local-agent MARL design, explicit communication and PPO details, field-derived inputs, reproducible training setup and direct FDMARL comparison; limitations are only partially discussed through scalability/non-stationarity and simulation-only validation.

Clear multi-agent irrigation architecture, sensing/actuation roles, real-weather case-study inputs, detailed evapotranspiration equations and a conventional-pivot comparison showing water reduction; however, the paper does not meaningfully discuss limitations or threats to validity.

Clear harvest-workforce problem, worker/auction roles and allocation mechanisms, large commercial-farm dataset, explicit historical/live experiments with statistical testing, strong methodological detail, and substantial discussion of simulation/data/deployment limitations and future field trials.
Clear RL agents and CRSS coupling, strong real-data/simulation evaluation, public code/data and explicit uncertainty/data/model limitations.

Clear climate-adaptation objective and farmer-agent decision model, well-described climate/economic inputs and extensive scenario simulation with explicit limitations; inter-agent communication/coordination is only partial because direct farmer interaction and mutual learning are not implemented in the prototype.

Clear environmental-policy objective, farm/transport-agent structure and interaction, full-population administrative dataset, detailed MP formulation and validation, meaningful policy/investment evaluation, and explicit discussion of normative/static modelling limitations and future extensions.

Clear MAPDES objective, farm/auction roles and P2P coordination with meaningful one-year comparative simulation; reproducibility is only partial in this short paper because implementation/data details are limited, and limitations are mainly addressed through brief future-work notes.
Clear resource-allocation formulation and evaluation; reproducibility is good mathematically but implementation/data artefacts are not provided in the paper; limitations/future work are explicit.

Clear heterogeneous-agent/task objective, detailed HBCA auction mechanism, explicit uncertainty scenarios and strong comparative simulation across 36 instances; methodology is reproducible, but the paper does not meaningfully discuss study limitations or threats to validity.

Clear farmer-agent/resource-sharing model and environment-mediated coordination, real Lake Koronia calibration plus systematic simulations, detailed learning equations and meaningful environmental/farmer outcomes; simplifying assumptions are described but there is no comprehensive limitations discussion.

Very detailed worker/picker/runner agent roles, auction and team-allocation mechanisms, historic/live commercial-farm data, statistical comparisons and realistic multi-scale simulations; limitations of incomplete data, computation and non-deployment plus extensive future work are explicitly discussed.

Clear worker-team allocation objective, GA/auction mechanisms, real 2021 commercial-farm data and statistically tested comparisons with manual and algorithmic baselines; methods are reproducible, while limitations are discussed mainly through run-time and planned field-trial/seasonal future work.

Clear platform objective and ODD-based agent architecture; explicit land/water markets and technology diffusion; rich empirical/biophysical inputs; multiple applications and validation tests; freeware, user guide and default test data are available; dedicated limitations section discusses actor scope and missing collective decision-making.

Clear policy objective, heterogeneous farm-agent decisions and IPM diffusion; survey-based inputs and validation against land use, revenue and pesticide use; downloadable implementation/input files; systematic scenario comparisons and explicit discussion of behavioural and pest-ecology limitations.

Detailed MP-MAS/TSPC architecture, farm-agent/network interactions, survey and soil data, explicit validation and long-horizon scenario analysis; executable/input files are documented; discussion clearly identifies behavioural simplification, transferred conservation parameters and sensitivity to yield assumptions.

Clear cooperation objective, farmer/network/government entities and neighbourhood coordination; extensive survey calibration and 3.84 million simulation runs with robust regressions; NetLogo model is publicly available. Limitations are mainly implicit/stylised rather than presented as a comprehensive limitations analysis.

Clear socio-agricultural collective-action objective, farmer autonomy and shared-aquifer interaction; equations, parameterisation and systematic climate/behaviour scenarios are detailed. Model assumptions and simplifications are described, but there is no dedicated comprehensive limitations section or accessible code/data artifact.

Clear coupled farmer–watershed objective, Bayesian adaptation and neighbour information exchange; calibrated SWAT environment plus sensitivity and behavioural comparisons. Reproducibility is reduced because the full farmer decision model is partly deferred to a thesis and no code/data package is provided; validation challenges and future empirical needs are explicitly discussed.

Clear objective and agent/government roles; explicit cooperation/management mechanisms; detailed Doroudzan case data and wet/normal/drought evaluation with ABM-before/after and optimisation comparisons. Reproducibility reduced because no accessible code/data package is provided. Limitations and need for dynamic behavioural models are explicit.

Clear MAELIA agricultural-model objective, farmer decision rules, hydrological/normative coupling and empirical withdrawal/practice validation. Detailed data sources and eight-year evaluation. Reproducibility limited by no accessible study code/data package. Limitations and future improvements are explicit.

Foundational but technically detailed MAS–CA model with explicit farm interactions, markets, hydrology, empirical calibration and robustness/scenario evaluation. Software implementation and model structure are described in detail, supporting strong methodological reproducibility even though no modern repository is provided. Limitations are discussed but are scattered and not presented as a systematic limitations section.

Clear groundwater-management objective, detailed farmer/entity rules and direct/indirect interactions, field-based model construction, sensitivity/credibility assessment and management scenarios. Specific model code/data are not made readily accessible, reducing reproducibility. Unrealistic socio-economic mechanisms and validation needs are explicitly discussed.

Detailed CATCHSCAPE architecture, farmer/manager negotiation and integrated catchment representation with multiple scenario runs. Empirical authentication against crop maps/yields is useful but evaluation is explicitly exploratory and not a full predictive validation, so QA5=1. Model rules/platform and scenario procedure are described extensively; limitations/future stakeholder authentication are explicit.

Clear virtual-laboratory objective; explicit farmer/group agents, communication and collective rules; field-grounded environment; repeated stochastic scenario evaluation with stable viability classification. Reproducibility is reduced by lack of accessible code/data artifact. Heuristic purpose and need for external validation are clearly acknowledged.

Clear integrated bio-economic MAS objective, explicit farm-household decision rules and peer diffusion, rich survey/spatial/soil inputs, quantitative construct/result validation and policy scenarios. MP-MAS freeware/manual are reported available; validation limitations and omitted uncertainty/soil-sustainability needs are discussed explicitly.

Clear adaptive water-allocation objective, detailed 11-agent utilities/behaviour and scarcity coordination, rich hydrological/behavioural inputs, explicit comparisons of seven bankruptcy methods and fairness/profit metrics. Data are included in the paper/SI and limitations/future behavioural, social and negotiation extensions are extensive.

Clear large-scale irrigation MARA formulation, detailed agent/allocation constraints and LINTUL2/MPC method, 33-season heuristic comparison and uncertainty analysis. Reproducibility is reduced by absence of implementation code despite public model/weather data; full-state assumption, sensitivity and real-practice validation needs are explicit.

Clear multi-robot task-allocation objective and centralized INSGA-II coordination, with public benchmarks plus real farm task data and repeated algorithm comparisons. No code package is provided and the real-farm dataset is not clearly released; limitations are mainly brief future-work notes on Euclidean distance, real path planning and collision avoidance.

Clear participatory crop-livestock integration objective, detailed farm-agent/scenario coordination and multi-source real-farm data, 13-year baseline/scenario comparisons with participatory calibration/validation and supplementary data. The paper explicitly details modelling, context, environmental and transferability limitations and future extensions.

Clear multi-level WEF-nexus objective, detailed MAELIA/strategic architecture and resource coordination, large spatial case study and comparative AHP/Monte-Carlo/computational evaluation. Reproducibility is limited because data are available only on request and no study code package is provided; model incompleteness, indicator bias and future extensions are explicit.

Clear irrigation MARA/MPC objective, explicit resource-delivery agents and allocation constraints, public LINTUL2/weather basis and 33-season heuristic comparison. Reproducibility is reduced by lack of released controller code; full-state assumptions, omitted travel/inventory, parameter sensitivity and future distributed/real-world work are explicit.
